title: CV Linter distribution research: local executable, Agent Skill, and MCP
status: Research input; no installation, host experiment, or market result is claimed.
decision: MVP is one local Rust executable with a shared in-process core, CLI commands, and a stdio MCP adapter. There is no always-running HTTP backend.

mvp.executable: The CLI and cv-linter mcp --stdio call the same local Rust core.
cli: lint: deterministic parsing, spelling, formatting/structure, and literal checks
extract-text: explicit extraction of bounded, ordered text blocks with stable IDs
mcp_tools: extract_cv_text: the explicit extraction operation for host-AI analysis
mvp.boundary: MCP is a local process transport and distribution surface. It must not open an HTTP listener, become a daemon, or expose a generic filesystem, shell, URL, vendor, judge, or scoring tool.

pros: Provides concise routing, privacy, and citation instructions for compatible hosts.
Can point the host to a pinned executable without reproducing parsing logic in prompts.
limits: A skill is not an OS privacy boundary; host permissions still matter.
Host chat and model policies remain separate from local parsing.

pros: Offers typed discovery to technically comfortable Codex/Claude users.
Keeps deterministic operations in the local executable and reuses the same schemas and core.
Makes explicit extraction a clear handoff boundary for host-AI semantic analysis.
limits: MCP does not make the host model or chat local.
Client permissions, lifecycle, and result handling require conformance testing.
A stdio adapter does not justify a remote server or broader tool surface.

options.hypothesis: Non-agent users may value drag-and-drop and visual source inspection, but broad Swedish job-seeker demand is unverified.
options.reason: A browser client adds a second runtime, storage and bridge surface before observed user need justifies it.
Consider only after evidence from paying customers justifies a desktop distribution and its update/support burden.

mcp_position.acquisition_hypothesis: MCP-first may be an early-adopter wedge for technically comfortable Codex/Claude users.
mcp_position.what_it_does_not_prove: MCP adoption is not evidence of broad reach among Swedish job seekers, non-agent users, or paying customers.
mcp_position.validation: Measure installation, successful linting, useful citations, and retention with the target host before adding adapters or UI.

privacy_notes: Parsing and deterministic linting are local. Explicitly extracted CV text handed to a configured AI host enters that host's context and follows the host/model's policies.
The complete workflow is local only when the selected semantic model is local and verified not to forward data.
Read one user-selected file or supplied bytes; do not scan directories, fetch URLs, or follow embedded resources.
Keep raw CV bytes/text in process memory or explicit user-directed streams only. MVP has no raw-CV store, database, accounts, cloud sync, telemetry, or automatic history.
Do not claim that local stdio, an Agent Skill, or a local parser makes provider copies or host transcripts local.
deferred_features: always-running HTTP backend or localhost service
built-in LLM judge, scoring, ranking, and vendor profiles
cloud sync, Supabase CV storage, databases, accounts, authentication, billing, and analytics
durable history, broad export, automatic rewriting, OCR, grammar/tone systems, and broad ATS compatibility claims
